Nationhood
NAY-shun-hood
noun / doctrine
From Latin natio, “birth, people,” rendering Hebrew goy and Greek ethnos, a people bound by common descent, tongue, and bound habitation.

📖 Biblical Definition

Nationhood is the divine ordering of the human race into distinct peoples, made of one blood, set within appointed bounds, and gathered at last from every nation around the throne of the Lamb. Paul declares at Athens that God “hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation” (Act 17:26). The nations themselves are no accident of history but the work of the LORD, who at Babel scattered the families of the sons of Noah, “every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations” (Gen 10:32), and who “set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel” (Deu 32:8). Thus the existence of nations, with their borders, languages, and peoples, is a providential good, ordained for the dwelling and ordering of fallen men. Yet nationhood is never an ultimate. It serves a higher end, for the gospel goes out to all nations, and the redeemed are gathered as “a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues” (Rev 7:9). Every nation stands under the Lord Jesus Christ, who is King of kings; and the diversity of the peoples is not erased but redeemed, brought to bow before one Saviour and to praise one God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The divine ordering of mankind into distinct peoples, made of one blood within appointed bounds, gathered at last from every nation to Christ.

expand to see more

NATIONHOOD, the divinely ordained ordering of mankind into distinct peoples.

God made of one blood all nations and set the bounds of their habitation (Act 17:26).

The nations were divided after Babel, every one after his tongue (Gen 10:32).

The LORD set the bounds of the people in His providence (Deu 32:8).

The redeemed are gathered from all nations before the throne (Rev 7:9).

📖 Key Scripture

Act 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;"

Gen 10:32 — "These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations, in their nations: and by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood."

Deu 32:8 — "When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel."

Rev 7:9 — "After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Two errors assail biblical nationhood: the globalist erasure of nations, and the idolatrous ethno-nationalism that makes blood and soil an ultimate; Christ alone is Lord over all nations.

expand to see more

On the one hand stands the globalist erasure of nations, which treats borders, peoples, and tongues as relics to be dissolved into a single undifferentiated mass of humanity. This denies the work of God, who Himself divided the nations after Babel and set the bounds of their habitation. The diversity of the peoples is His ordering, not a problem to be abolished; to seek the melting of all nations into one earthly empire is to repeat the very sin of Babel, which the LORD came down to scatter.

On the other hand stands an idolatrous ethno-nationalism, which exalts blood and soil into an ultimate and makes a man’s people, rather than the Lord Jesus Christ, the object of his highest loyalty. This too is a corruption, for it forgets that God made of one blood all nations, that every nation stands under judgment, and that the redeemed are gathered from every kindred and tongue. The Christian loves his own people rightly, as a gift of providence, but he worships only Christ, before whom every nation must bow. Nationhood is a good servant and a damnable god; it must be kept under the lordship of the King of kings.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Latin natio, “a people,” rendering the Hebrew goy and Greek ethnos, the divinely bounded peoples of the earth.

expand to see more

Nationhood — from Latin natio, “birth, a people.”

It renders the Hebrew goy, a nation or people.

It renders the Greek ethnos, a nation, whence “ethnic.”

The nations were divided at Babel by the hand of God.

The redeemed are gathered from every nation to Christ.

Usage

"Love your own people as a gift of providence, but worship Christ alone, who is Lord over every nation."

"Reject the globalist dream of erasing the nations God Himself divided and bounded."

"Reject the idol of blood and soil, which sets a people above the King of kings."
